title.raw: 卷31 列傳第23 韋孝寬 韋敻 梁士彥 Volume 31 Biographies 23: Wei Xiaokuan; Wei Xiong; Liang Shiyan

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬 韋敻 梁士彥

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan; Wei Xiong; Liang Shiyan
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Xiong, and Liang Shiyan

sentences.zh: 韋叔裕字孝寬，京兆杜陵人也，少以字行。

translations.literal: Wei Shuyu, styled Xiaokuan, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao; from youth he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuyu, courtesy name Xiaokuan, came from Duling in Jingzhao commandery and was known from youth by his style rather than his given name.

sentences.zh: 世為三輔著姓。

translations.literal: For generations the family was a distinguished clan of the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they were a leading clan of the Three Adjuncts around Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 祖直善，魏馮翊、扶風二郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhishan served as administrator of Fenyang and Fufeng, the two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhishan had been administrator of both Fenyang and Fufeng commanderies under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父旭，武威郡守。

translations.literal: His father Xu was Administrator of Wuwei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu served as administrator of Wuwei commandery.

sentences.zh: 建義初，為大行臺右丞，加輔國將軍、雍州大中正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he was made Right Assistant of the Grand Commissionerate, with the added titles General Who Assists the State and Grand Rectifier of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he became right assistant of the grand commissionerate, with the additional titles General Who Assists the State and grand rectifier of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，拜右將軍、南

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongan, he was appointed General of the Right and southern
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongan he was made General of the Right and inspector of southern

translations.literal: (You) [emended: Bīn]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Bīn]

sentences.zh: 〔豳〕州刺史。

translations.literal: 〔Bīn〕 Province.
translations.idiomatic: Bīn Province.

sentences.zh: 時氐賊數為抄竊，旭隨機招撫，竝即歸附。

translations.literal: At the time Di bandits repeatedly raided and plundered; Xu, adapting to circumstances, won them over, and all at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Di raiders had been striking again and again; Xu met each case as it came, offering inducements, and they submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈司空、冀州刺史，諡曰文惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Minister of Works and Inspector of Ji Province; posthumous title Wen Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works and inspector of Ji, with the posthumous name Wen Hui.

sentences.zh: 孝寬沉敏和正，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was deep, keen, harmonious, and upright; he ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan was grave, quick-witted, even-tempered, and upright, with a working knowledge of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，屬蕭寶夤作亂關右，乃詣闕，請為軍前驅。

translations.literal: At the capping age, when Xiao Baoyin raised rebellion in the Guanzhong region, he went to the capital and asked to serve as vanguard of the army.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty, when Xiao Baoyin rebelled in the Guanzhong region, he went to court and volunteered to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，即拜統軍。

translations.literal: The court praised this and at once appointed him commander.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended his offer and immediately made him a corps commander.

sentences.zh: 隨馮翊公長孫承業西征，每戰有功。

translations.literal: He followed Duke of Fenyang Changsun Chengye on the western campaign; in every battle he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west under Duke of Fenyang Changsun Chengye and distinguished himself in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 拜國子博士，行華

translations.literal: Appointed Erudite of the National University, acting for Hua
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed erudite of the National University and given acting charge of Hua

translations.literal: (Yin) [emended: Shān]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Shān]

sentences.zh: 〔山〕郡事。

translations.literal: 〔Shān〕 commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: commandery affairs.

sentences.zh: 屬侍中楊侃為大都督，出鎮潼關，引孝寬為司馬。

translations.literal: When Attendant-in-Ordinary Yang Kan became grand area commander and went out to garrison Tong Pass, he brought Xiaokuan in as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When palace attendant Yang Kan was made grand area commander and posted to Tong Pass, he took Xiaokuan on as his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 侃奇其才，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Kan marveled at his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, struck by his ability, gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 永安中，授宣威將軍、給事中，尋賜爵山北縣男。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was granted General Who Proclaims Might and Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon enfeoffed Baron of Shanbei county.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan he received the titles General Who Proclaims Might and gentleman attendant-in-ordinary, and was soon enfeoffed Baron of Shanbei.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，以都督從荊州刺史源子恭鎮襄城，以功除

translations.literal: In Putai, as area commander he followed Inspector of Jing Province Yuan Zigong in garrisoning Xiangcheng; for merit he was removed as
translations.idiomatic: In Putai he served as area commander under Inspector of Jing Yuan Zigong at the Xiangcheng garrison and, for merit, was appointed

translations.literal: (Zhè) [emended: Xī]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Xī]

sentences.zh: 〔析〕陽郡守。

translations.literal: 〔Xī〕yang commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: administrator of Xiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 時獨孤信為新野郡守，

translations.literal: At that time Dugu Xin was Administrator of Xinye commandery,
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dugu Xin was administrator of Xinye commandery,

translations.literal: (Sī) [emended: Tóng]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Tóng]

sentences.zh: 〔同〕荊州，與孝寬情好款密，政術俱美，荊部吏人，號為聯璧。

translations.literal: 〔Tóng〕 Jing Province; with Xiaokuan friendship was warm and close, and in governance both were excellent; officials and people of Jing called them the Twin Jades.
translations.idiomatic: and also of Jing Province; he and Xiaokuan were close as brothers, and both governed with distinction — the people of Jing spoke of them as paired jades.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，以都督鎮城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, as area commander he garrisoned the city.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he garrisoned the city as area commander.

sentences.zh: 文帝自原州赴雍州，命孝寬隨軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen came from Yuan Province to Yong Province; he ordered Xiaokuan to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai marched from Yuan Province to Yong Province, Xiaokuan was ordered to accompany the army.

sentences.zh: 及剋潼關，即授弘農郡守。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass was taken, he was at once appointed Administrator of Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tong Pass fell, he was immediately made administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，兼左丞，節度宜陽兵馬事。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dou Tai, he was additionally made Left Assistant and directed the troops and horses of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Tai was taken, he was also made left assistant and put in charge of the forces at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 仍與獨孤信入洛陽城守。

translations.literal: He again entered Luoyang with Dugu Xin to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Luoyang again with Dugu Xin to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 復與宇文貴、怡峰應接潁州義徒，破東魏將任祥、堯雄於潁川。

translations.literal: Again with Yuwen Gui and Yi Feng he answered the call of the righteous bands of Ying Province and defeated Eastern Wei generals Ren Xiang and Yao Xiong at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again with Yuwen Gui and Yi Feng to support the loyalists of Ying Province and routed the Eastern Wei commanders Ren Xiang and Yao Xiong at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 孝寬又進平樂口，下豫州，獲刺史馮邕。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan again advanced and pacified Lekou, descended on Yuzhou, and captured Inspector Feng Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan pushed on to secure Lekou, took Yuzhou, and captured its inspector, Feng Yong.

sentences.zh: 又從戰於河橋。

translations.literal: He again followed in battle at He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at He Bridge.

sentences.zh: 時大軍不利，邊境騷然，乃令孝寬以大將軍行宜陽郡事。

translations.literal: At that time the great army met with misfortune; the borderlands were in turmoil, and Xiaokuan was ordered to act as Grand General and administer Yiyang commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force suffered defeat and the frontier shook, Xiaokuan was ordered to serve as acting grand general and administer Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Inspector of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to inspector of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東魏將段琛、堯傑復據宜陽，遣其

translations.literal: That year, Eastern Wei generals Duan Chen and Yao Jie again held Yiyang; they sent their
translations.idiomatic: That year the Eastern Wei generals Duan Chen and Yao Jie reoccupied Yiyang and sent their

translations.literal: (Yáng) [emended: Yáng]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Yáng]

sentences.zh: 〔陽〕州刺史牛道恒扇誘邊民。

translations.literal: 〔Yáng〕 Province inspector Niu Daoheng to incite and lure the border people.
translations.idiomatic: inspector of Yang Province, Niu Daoheng, to win over the frontier population.

sentences.zh: 孝寬深患之，乃遣諜人訪獲道恒手跡，令善學書者偽作道恒與孝寬書，論歸款意，又為落燼燒跡，若火下書者，還令諜人送於琛營。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan deeply worried over this; he then sent spies who obtained Daoheng's handwriting, ordered men skilled at calligraphy to forge a letter from Daoheng to Xiaokuan discussing surrender, and also burned the edges with fallen embers as if the letter had been written under fire; he then had the spies deliver it to Chen's camp.
translations.idiomatic: The situation troubled Xiaokuan deeply. He sent agents who obtained samples of Daoheng's hand, had a skilled calligrapher forge a letter from Daoheng to Xiaokuan proposing defection, singed the edges with embers as though the note had been written amid fire, and sent the agents to deliver it to Chen's camp.

sentences.zh: 琛得書，果疑道恒，其所欲經略，皆不見用。

translations.literal: Chen received the letter and indeed grew suspicious of Daoheng; the plans he wished to carry out were none of them adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen read the letter and came to distrust Daoheng; none of the schemes he had in mind was put into effect.

sentences.zh: 孝寬知其離阻，日出奇兵掩襲，擒道恒及琛等，崤、澠遂清。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, knowing they were divided and obstructed, each day sent surprise troops in raids; he captured Daoheng, Chen, and the rest, and the Xiao and Mian regions were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiaokuan saw the rift between them, he sent raiding parties out daily by surprise, captured Daoheng and Chen, and cleared the Xiao and Mian corridor.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong, he was advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉晉州刺史，尋移鎮玉壁，兼攝南汾州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Inspector of Jin Province; soon he moved his garrison to Yubi and concurrently administered Southern Fen Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made inspector of Jin, then shifted his headquarters to Yubi while also overseeing Southern Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 先是山胡負險，屢為劫盜，孝寬示以威信，州境肅然。

translations.literal: Earlier the mountain Hu had relied on the terrain's defiles and repeatedly raided; Xiaokuan displayed authority and good faith, and the province's borders became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain Hu had long used the rough country to raid at will; Xiaokuan combined firmness with trust, and the province settled.

sentences.zh: 進授大都督。

translations.literal: He was further appointed grand area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 十二年，齊神武傾山東之眾，志圖西入，以玉壁沖要，先命攻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Gao Huan mustered the hosts of Shandong, intending to drive west; because Yubi was strategically vital, he ordered it attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Gao Huan gathered the armies of the east with the aim of pushing west; Yubi stood on the critical line, and he struck there first.

sentences.zh: 連營數十里，至於城下，乃於城南起土山，欲乘之以入。

translations.literal: He linked camps for several tens of li, reaching below the walls; then at the south of the city he raised an earthen mound, intending to ride it into the city.
translations.idiomatic: His camps stretched for tens of li to the foot of the walls; south of the city he piled an earthen mound, planning to roll over the ramparts on its height.

sentences.zh: 當其山處，城上先有兩高樓。

translations.literal: Where the mound was to rise, the walls already had two tall towers.
translations.idiomatic: On the very ground where the mound was rising, the defenders already held two high towers.

sentences.zh: 孝寬更縛木接之，命極高峻，多積戰具以禦之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan bound timber and extended them, ordering them made extremely high and steep, and piled many weapons of war to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan lashed timbers to the towers and raised them still higher, stacking arms and engines on the platforms to meet the assault.

sentences.zh: 齊神武使謂城中曰：「縱爾縛樓至天，我會穿城取爾。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sent word to the city, saying: "Even if you bind your towers to the sky, I will still tunnel through the wall and take you.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent a message into the city: "Bind your towers to the heavens if you like — I will still bore under your wall and take you.

sentences.zh: 」遂於城南鑿地道。

translations.literal: " He then dug a tunnel at the south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he opened a tunnel south of the walls.

sentences.zh: 又於城北起土山，攻具，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Again at the north of the city he raised an earthen mound and siege engines, attacking day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city he raised another mound and siege engines, pressing the attack day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 孝寬復掘長塹，要其地道，仍飭戰士屯塹。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan again dug a long trench to intercept the tunnel and ordered warriors stationed in the trench.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan countered by cutting a long trench across the tunnel's path and posting fighters along it.

sentences.zh: 城外每穿至塹，戰士即擒殺之。

translations.literal: Each time the enemy outside broke through to the trench, the warriors at once seized and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the diggers broke through into the trench, the men waiting there killed them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又於塹外積柴貯火，敵人有伏地道內者，便下柴火，以皮韝吹之。

translations.literal: Again outside the trench he piled firewood and stored fire; when enemies lay hidden in the tunnel, they dropped fire and firewood and blew with leather bellows.
translations.idiomatic: He also piled brush and kindling beyond the trench; when enemies crouched in the tunnel, the defenders dropped fire and fanned the flames with leather bellows.

sentences.zh: 吹氣一沖，咸即灼爛。

translations.literal: One blast of air, and all were at once scorched and burned.
translations.idiomatic: One gust of forced air, and the men below were burned to cinders.

sentences.zh: 城外又造攻車，車之所及，莫不摧毀。

translations.literal: Outside the walls they also built assault towers; wherever the towers reached, nothing failed to be smashed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls they built assault towers whose reach shattered everything they struck.

sentences.zh: 雖有排楯，莫之能抗。

translations.literal: Though there were shield-walls, none could resist.
translations.idiomatic: Even the shield-walls could not hold them off.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃縫布為縵，隨其所向則張設之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then sewed cloth into awnings and, wherever the towers aimed, spread them out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had cloth sewn into awnings and spread them wherever the towers bore.

sentences.zh: 布既懸於空中，其車竟不能壞。

translations.literal: Once the cloth hung in midair, the towers could not destroy it after all.
translations.idiomatic: Suspended in the air, the cloth baffled the towers and they could not break through.

sentences.zh: 城外又縛松於竿，灌油加火，規以燒布，并欲焚樓。

translations.literal: Outside the walls they again bound pine to poles, poured on oil and added fire, planning to burn the cloth and also to burn the towers.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers next lashed pine to poles, soaked them in oil, and set them alight, hoping to burn away the cloth and the towers together.

sentences.zh: 孝寬復長作鐵鉤，利其鋒刃，火竿來，以鉤遙割之，松麻俱落。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan again made long iron hooks with sharpened blades; when the fire-poles came, he cut them off at a distance with the hooks, and pine and hemp alike fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan answered with long iron hooks sharpened to an edge; as the fire-poles advanced, men at a distance hooked and cut them away, and pine and tow fell together.

sentences.zh: 外又於城四面穿地，作二十一道，分為四路，於其中各施樑柱，作訖，以油灌柱，放火燒之，柱折，城并崩壞。

translations.literal: Outside they again dug into the earth on the city's four sides, making twenty-one tunnels in four routes; within each they set beams and pillars, and when finished poured oil on the pillars and set fire; the pillars broke and the walls collapsed together.
translations.idiomatic: They dug twenty-one galleries in four directions around the walls, propped each with beams and posts, then soaked the posts in oil and burned them; the posts snapped and whole sections of wall came down.

sentences.zh: 孝寬又隨崩處豎木柵以扞之，敵不得入。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan again erected wooden palisades wherever the walls collapsed to block them; the enemy could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the wall gave way, Xiaokuan threw up wooden palisades; the enemy could not pass.

sentences.zh: 城外盡其攻擊之術，孝寬咸拒破之。

translations.literal: Outside the walls they exhausted every method of attack; Xiaokuan repelled and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers spent every art of assault; Xiaokuan turned each one aside.

sentences.zh: 神武無如之何，乃遣倉曹參軍祖孝徵謂曰：「未聞救兵，何不降也？

translations.literal: Gao Huan could do nothing about it; he then sent Registrar Zu Xiaozheng to say: "Relief has not been heard of — why not surrender?
translations.idiomatic: At his wits' end, Gao Huan sent registrar Zu Xiaozheng to say, "No relief has come — why not surrender?

sentences.zh: 」孝寬報云：「我城池嚴固，兵食有餘，攻者自勞，守者常逸。

translations.literal: " Xiaokuan replied: "My walls and moat are stern and solid; soldiers and grain are in surplus; those who attack grow weary of themselves, while those who defend remain at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaokuan answered, "Our walls are strong, our stores ample; the attackers wear themselves out while the defenders rest.

sentences.zh: 豈有旬朔之間，已須救援。

translations.literal: How could relief already be needed within a ten-day or month-long span?
translations.idiomatic: Relief within a fortnight or a month? Hardly.

sentences.zh: 適憂爾眾有不反之危。

translations.literal: I only worry that your masses face the danger of men who will not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: I worry rather for your host — that some among you may not live to turn home.

sentences.zh: 孝寬關西男子，必不為降將軍也。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan is a man of Guanxi; he will certainly not become a surrendering general.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of the western passes; I will not be a general who surrenders.

sentences.zh: 」俄而孝徵復謂城中人曰：「韋城主受彼榮祿，或復可爾，自外軍士，何事相隨入湯火中耶。

translations.literal: " Before long Xiaozheng again said to the people in the city: "Commandant Wei receives their honors and salary — perhaps that can be forgiven; as for the rest of you soldiers, why follow him into boiling water and fire?
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Xiaozheng called to the garrison: "Your commandant enjoys their pay and rank — perhaps he has his reasons; but you other soldiers — why follow him into fire?

sentences.zh: 」乃射募格於城中云：「能斬城主降者，拜太尉，封開國郡公，邑萬戶，賞帛萬疋。

translations.literal: " He then shot a recruitment placard into the city, saying: "Whoever can behead the commandant and surrender will be appointed Grand Commandant, enfeoffed Duke of the State-Founding Commandery with a fief of ten thousand households, and rewarded with ten thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " He shot a bounty notice into the city: "Slay the commandant and come over, and you shall be made grand commandant, enfeoffed Duke of the State-Founding Commandery with ten thousand households, and given ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 」孝寬手題書背，反射城外云：「若有斬高歡者，一依此賞。

translations.literal: " Xiaokuan wrote on the back with his own hand and shot it back outside the walls, saying: "If anyone beheads Gao Huan, the reward will follow this notice exactly.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaokuan wrote on the back in his own hand and shot the notice back out: "Behead Gao Huan, and the same reward stands.

sentences.zh: 」孝寬弟子遷，先在山東，又鎖至城下，臨以白刃，云若不早降，便行大戮。

translations.literal: " Xiaokuan's nephew Qian had earlier been in Shandong and was again chained and brought below the walls; they held naked blades over him, saying that if he did not surrender soon, mass execution would follow.
translations.idiomatic: " His nephew Qian, who had been in the east, was dragged in chains to the foot of the wall; blades were laid to his throat with the promise that unless the city surrendered at once, he would be slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 孝寬慷慨激揚，略無顧意。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was impassioned and roused, with scarcely a glance of concern.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan answered with fierce resolve and never so much as wavered.

sentences.zh: 士卒莫不感勵，人有死難之心。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were all moved and inspired; each man had the heart to die in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers alike took fire from him; every man found the will to die where he stood.

sentences.zh: 神武苦戰六旬，傷及病死者十四五，智力俱困，因而發疾。

translations.literal: Gao Huan fought bitterly for sixty days; the wounded and sick who died were four or five in ten; wit and strength were both exhausted, and he thereupon fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan hammered at the city for sixty days; four or five men in ten fell wounded or dead; mind and body gave out together, and he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 其夜遁去。

translations.literal: That night he fled away.
translations.idiomatic: That night he stole away.

sentences.zh: 後因此忿恚，遂殂。

translations.literal: Afterward, because of this resentment and rage, he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: The humiliation rankled; he died not long after.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝嘉孝寬功，令殿中尚書長孫紹遠、左丞王悅至玉壁勞問，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵建忠郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei commended Xiaokuan's merit and ordered Palace Secretary Changsun Shaoyuan and Left Assistant Wang Yue to come to Yubi with condolences; he was granted General of Agile Cavalry, Opener of the Way with the Three Precedence, and advanced in rank to Duke of the Commandery of Established Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei honored Xiaokuan's service and sent palace secretary Changsun Shaoyuan and left assistant Wang Yue to Yubi with imperial praise; Xiaokuan was made General of Agile Cavalry and opener of the way with the three precedences, and raised to Duke of the Commandery of Established Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei, he was made Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei he was appointed inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 先是，路側一里置一土候，經雨頹毀，每須修之。

translations.literal: Earlier, along the roads one earth beacon had been placed every li; beaten by rain they collapsed and were ruined, and each time repair was needed.
translations.idiomatic: Until then the highways had been marked every li by earthen beacon-mounds; rain washed them down and they had to be rebuilt again and again.

sentences.zh: 自孝寬臨州，乃勒部內當候處植槐樹代之。

translations.literal: From the time Xiaokuan took the province, he ordered that wherever beacons were required within his jurisdiction, locust trees be planted in their place.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaokuan took office he ordered locust trees planted wherever the route called for a beacon within his province.

sentences.zh: 既免修復，行旅又得庇蔭。

translations.literal: Repair was thus avoided, and travelers also gained shade.
translations.idiomatic: Repairs ceased, and travelers gained shade into the bargain.

sentences.zh: 周文後見，怪問知之，曰：「豈得一州獨爾，當令天下同之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai later saw this, wondered and asked how it was known, and said: "How can one province alone be thus — it should be made the same throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai later noticed the practice, asked how it had come about, and said, "One province should not have this alone — let the whole realm follow suit.

sentences.zh: 」於是令諸州夾道一里種一樹，十里種三樹，百里種五樹焉。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered that in every province one tree be planted every li along the roads, three trees every ten li, and five trees every hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered every province to plant one tree per li along the highways, three per ten li, and five per hundred li.

sentences.zh: 保定初，以孝寬立勳玉壁，遂於玉壁置勳州，仍授勳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, because Xiaokuan had established merit at Yubi, Xun Province was therefore established at Yubi; he was still appointed Inspector of Xun Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding, in recognition of Xiaokuan's stand at Yubi, Merit Province was created at Yubi and he was made its inspector.

sentences.zh: 齊人遣使至玉壁，求通互市。

translations.literal: The men of Qi sent envoys to Yubi requesting mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent envoys to Yubi to ask for border markets.

sentences.zh: 晉公護以其相持日久，絕無使命，一日忽來求交易，疑別有故。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, because the two sides had faced each other for a long time with absolutely no missions, and on a single day suddenly came seeking trade, suspected there was some other reason.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu noted that after long stalemate without a single envoy, Qi had suddenly asked to trade and suspected some hidden design.

sentences.zh: 又以皇姑、皇世母先沒在彼，因其請和之際，或可致之。

translations.literal: Also, because the emperor's aunt and the emperor's consort's mother had earlier died in captivity there, at the time of this request for peace it might perhaps be possible to recover them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's aunt and his consort's mother had died in Qi custody; during talks for peace their remains might be recovered.

sentences.zh: 遂令司門下大夫尹公正至玉壁，共孝寬詳議。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered Supervisor of the Gate and Lower Grandee Yin Gongzheng to go to Yubi and discuss the matter in detail with Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent supervisor of the gate and lower grandee Yin Gongzheng to Yubi to work out the details with Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃於郊盛設供帳，令公正接對使人，兼論皇家親屬在東之意。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then set out a lavish pavilion in the suburbs and ordered Gongzheng to receive and answer the envoys, also raising the matter of imperial kin held in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan pitched a grand pavilion in the suburbs and had Gongzheng receive the envoys, raising as well the question of royal kin held in the east.

sentences.zh: 使者辭色甚悅。

translations.literal: The envoys' words and bearing were very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys received the overture with evident satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 時又有汾州胡抄得關東人，孝寬復放東還，並致書一牘，具陳朝廷欲敦鄰好。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Fen Province Hu who in raiding had captured men from east of the Pass; Xiaokuan again released them to return east and also sent a letter setting forth in full the court's wish to cultivate neighborly good relations.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu raiders from Fen Province had taken captives from east of the Pass, Xiaokuan freed them to go home and sent a letter stating the court's desire for good relations with its neighbor.

sentences.zh: 遂以禮送皇姑及護母等。

translations.literal: Thereupon with ceremony they sent back the emperor's aunt and Hu's mother and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Qi then ceremonially returned the emperor's aunt, Yuwen Hu's mother, and the others.

sentences.zh: 孝寬善於撫御，能得人心。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was skilled at winning men and keeping their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had a gift for winning loyalty and holding it.

sentences.zh: 所遣間諜入齊者，皆為盡力。

translations.literal: Every spy he sent into Qi exerted himself to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Every agent he sent into Qi served him with full devotion.

sentences.zh: 亦有齊人得孝寬金貨，遙通書疏。

translations.literal: There were also men of Qi who received gold and goods from Xiaokuan and communicated with him by letters from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Some men in Qi also took gold and goods from Xiaokuan and kept up a distant correspondence with him.

sentences.zh: 故齊動靜，朝廷皆先知。

translations.literal: Thus Qi's movements and stillness—the court always knew beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the court always learned of Qi's movements before they happened.

sentences.zh: 時有主帥許盆，孝寬托以心膂，令守一戍。

translations.literal: At the time there was garrison commander Xu Pen; Xiaokuan entrusted him as heart and backbone and had him guard one fortress.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a garrison commander, Xu Pen, whom Xiaokuan treated as a trusted right hand and posted to hold one fort.

sentences.zh: 盆乃以城東入。

translations.literal: Pen then entered through the east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Pen then went over to the enemy through the east of the city.

sentences.zh: 孝寬怒，遣諜取之，俄而斬首而還。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was angry; he sent spies to capture him, and before long beheaded him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan was furious. He sent agents to seize him, and soon had his head cut off and brought back.

sentences.zh: 其能致物情如此。

translations.literal: Such was his ability to win over popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his power to command loyalty and turn events his way.

sentences.zh: 汾州之北，離石以南，悉是生胡，抄掠居人，阻斷河路。

translations.literal: North of Fen Province and south of Lishi—all were raw Hu, raiding inhabitants and blocking river routes.
translations.idiomatic: North of Fen Province and south of Lishi lived wild Hu tribes who plundered the settled population and cut the river routes.

sentences.zh: 孝寬深患之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan was deeply troubled by the situation.

sentences.zh: 而地入于齊，無方誅剪。

translations.literal: But the territory had fallen to Qi; there was no means to suppress and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: But the land had passed to Qi, and he had no way to root them out.

sentences.zh: 欲當其要處，置一大城。

translations.literal: He wished to place a great city at a strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to build a major fortress at the key point.

sentences.zh: 乃於河西徵役徒十萬，甲士百人，遣開府姚岳監築之。

translations.literal: He then requisitioned one hundred thousand corvée laborers west of the river and one hundred armored soldiers, and sent Kaifu Yao Yue to supervise construction.
translations.idiomatic: He requisitioned a hundred thousand corvée laborers west of the river and a hundred armored troops, and sent Kaifu Yao Yue to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 岳色懼，以兵少為難。

translations.literal: Yue showed fear in his expression, citing the small number of troops as a difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yue looked alarmed and said there were too few soldiers for the task.

sentences.zh: 孝寬曰：「計成此城，十日即畢。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan said: "Calculate on completing this city—in ten days it will be done.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan said, "By my reckoning this fort can be finished in ten days.

sentences.zh: 既去晉州四百餘里，一日創手，二日偽境始知；

translations.literal: It is over four hundred li from Jin Province; one day to begin work, on the second day the false border will first learn of it;
translations.idiomatic: It is more than four hundred li from Jin Province. One day to break ground; on the second day the enemy will first hear of it.

sentences.zh: 設令晉州徵兵，二日方集；

translations.literal: Suppose Jin Province mobilizes troops—it takes two days to assemble;
translations.idiomatic: Even if Jin Province mobilizes, two days will pass before troops gather.

sentences.zh: 謀議之間，自稽三日；

translations.literal: Between deliberation and decision, that itself costs three days;
translations.idiomatic: Debate and planning will eat up three days on their own.

sentences.zh: 計其軍行，二日不到。

translations.literal: Counting their army's march, two days they will not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Count two more days for the march, and they still will not arrive.

sentences.zh: 我之城隍，足得辦矣。

translations.literal: Our ramparts will be quite finished.
translations.idiomatic: By then our walls will be ready.

sentences.zh: 」乃令築之。

translations.literal: " Then he ordered construction.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he ordered the building to begin.

sentences.zh: 齊人果至南首，疑有大軍，乃停留不進。

translations.literal: The men of Qi indeed reached the southern end, suspected a large army was present, and halted without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi troops did reach the south end, but fearing a large army they halted and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 其夜，又令汾水以南，傍介山、稷山諸村，所在縱火。

translations.literal: That night, he again had them set fires everywhere in villages south of the Fen River near Jie Mountain, Ji Mountain, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: That night he had fires lit in every village south of the Fen, around Jie Mountain, Ji Mountain, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 齊人謂是軍營，遂收兵自固。

translations.literal: The men of Qi took it for military camps and so withdrew their troops to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces took the fires for encampments and pulled back to consolidate their position.

sentences.zh: 版築克就，卒如其言。

translations.literal: The wall-building was completed; in the end it happened as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: The fortifications were finished, exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 四年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護將東討，孝寬遣長史辛道憲啟陳不可，護不納。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Jin Hu was about to campaign east; Xiaokuan sent chief administrator Xin Daoxian to memorialize that it should not be done; Hu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was preparing an eastern campaign, Xiaokuan sent his chief administrator Xin Daoxian to argue against it, but Hu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既而大軍果不利。

translations.literal: Before long the great army indeed fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the main army did suffer defeat.

sentences.zh: 後孔城遂陷，宜陽被圍。

translations.literal: Later Kongcheng fell, and Yiyang was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kongcheng fell and Yiyang came under siege.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃謂其將帥曰：「宜陽一城之地，未能損益。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then told his generals: "The territory of one city, Yiyang, cannot increase or decrease [our strength].
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan then told his commanders, "Yiyang is only one city; holding or losing it will not greatly change our strength.

sentences.zh: 然兩國爭之，勞師數載。

translations.literal: Yet the two states contend for it, exhausting armies for years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two states have fought over it for years, wearing out their armies.

sentences.zh: 彼多君子，寕乏謀猷。

translations.literal: They have many worthy men—surely they are not lacking in plans.
translations.idiomatic: Qi has no shortage of able men and stratagems.

sentences.zh: 若棄崤東，來圖汾北，我之疆界，必見侵擾。

translations.literal: If they abandon the east of Xiao and come to scheme at the north of Fen, our borders will surely suffer incursions.
translations.idiomatic: If they give up the east of Xiao and turn to the north bank of the Fen, our frontier will surely be harassed.

sentences.zh: 今宜於華谷及長秋速築城，以杜賊志。

translations.literal: Now we should quickly build cities at Huagu and Changqiu to block the enemy's intent.
translations.idiomatic: We should quickly fortify Huagu and Changqiu to block their designs.

sentences.zh: 脫其先我，圖之實難。

translations.literal: If they get ahead of us, it will truly be hard to counter their plans.
translations.idiomatic: If they move first, it will be very hard to stop them.

sentences.zh: 」於是畫地形，具陳其狀。

translations.literal: " Then he drew the terrain and fully set forth the situation.
translations.idiomatic: " He then mapped the ground and laid out the whole situation in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 晉公護令長史叱羅協謂使人曰：「韋公子孫雖多，數不滿百。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu had chief administrator Chiluo Xie tell the envoy: "Although Wei's sons and grandsons are many, their number does not reach a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Hu had his chief administrator Chiluo Xie tell the messenger, "The Wei clan may have many sons and grandsons, but they number fewer than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 汾北築城，遣誰固守？

translations.literal: For building cities on the north of Fen—whom will you send to hold them?
translations.idiomatic: If you build forts north of the Fen, who will you leave to hold them?"

sentences.zh: 」事遂不行。

translations.literal: " The matter then was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 天和五年，進爵鄖國公，增邑通前一萬戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe, he was raised to Duke of the State of Yun, with fief increased to ten thousand households in all including prior holdings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianhe he was made Duke of Yun, with his fief brought to ten thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 是歲，齊人果解宜陽之圍，經略汾北，遂築城守之。

translations.literal: That year, the men of Qi indeed lifted the siege of Yiyang, made moves on the north of Fen, and built cities to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qi did lift the siege of Yiyang, turned to the north bank of the Fen, and built forts to hold the ground.

sentences.zh: 其丞相斛律明月至汾東，請與孝寬相見。

translations.literal: Their chief minister Hulü Mingyue came to the east of Fen and requested to meet Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's chief minister Hulü Mingyue came to the east bank of the Fen and asked to meet Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 明月云：「宜陽小城，久勞戰爭。

translations.literal: Mingyue said: "Yiyang is a small city, long wearied by warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue said, "Yiyang is a small place, worn down by long fighting.

sentences.zh: 今既入彼，欲於汾北取償，幸勿怪也。

translations.literal: Now that we have taken it, we wish to take compensation on the north of Fen—please do not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we hold it, we mean to take compensation on the north bank of the Fen. Please do not be offended.

sentences.zh: 」孝寬答曰：「宜陽彼之要衝，汾北我之所棄。

translations.literal: " Xiaokuan replied: "Yiyang is their strategic pass; the north of Fen is what we have abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaokuan replied, "Yiyang is your vital pass. The north bank of the Fen is land we have already given up.

sentences.zh: 我棄彼圖，取償安在？

translations.literal: We abandoned it and they scheme—where is the compensation?
translations.idiomatic: We yielded it and you press further—where is the compensation in that?"

sentences.zh: 且君輔翼幼主，位重望隆，理宜調陰陽，撫百姓，焉用極武窮兵，構怨連禍！

translations.literal: Moreover you assist and support a young lord, your rank heavy and prestige lofty—you ought by rights to harmonize yin and yang and soothe the people. Why use utmost force and exhaust armies, heaping grudges and linking calamities!
translations.idiomatic: You stand beside a young ruler, high in rank and renown. You ought to harmonize the realm and comfort the people. Why exhaust armies in endless war and pile up hatred and disaster?"

sentences.zh: 且滄、瀛大水，千里無煙，復欲使汾、晉之間，橫屍暴骨？

translations.literal: Moreover the great floods at Cang and Ying—for a thousand li no smoke; and you would again make between Fen and Jin corpses lying across the land and bones exposed?
translations.idiomatic: Floods have already laid waste to Cang and Ying for a thousand li without a hearth-fire. Must you also fill the land between Fen and Jin with corpses and exposed bones?"

sentences.zh: 苟貪尋常之地，塗炭疲弊之人，竊為君不取。

translations.literal: If you would greedily seize ordinary territory and blacken and torment exhausted people—I venture it is not something you should do.
translations.idiomatic: To grasp at ordinary ground and grind down a people already spent—I do not think that suits a man of your standing."

sentences.zh: 」孝寬參軍曲岩頗知卜筮，謂孝寬曰：「來年，東朝必大相殺戮。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's aide Qu Yan was well versed in divination and oracle-bone reading; he told Xiaokuan: "Next year the Eastern Court will surely see great mutual slaying.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan's staff officer Qu Yan, who knew divination well, told him, "Next year the Eastern Court will surely see great bloodshed among its own."

sentences.zh: 」孝寬因令岩作謠歌曰：「百升飛上天，明月照長安。

translations.literal: " Xiaokuan therefore had Yan compose a ballad saying: "A hundred sheng fly up to heaven; the bright moon illuminates Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan then had Yan compose a rhyme: "A hundred sheng fly up to heaven; the bright moon shines on Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 」百升，斛也。

translations.literal: " "Hundred sheng" means hu.
translations.idiomatic: "Hundred sheng" is a pun on hu, the measure word for grain—and on Hulü.

sentences.zh: 又言：「高山不摧自崩，槲樹不扶自豎。

translations.literal: He also said: "High mountains without being shattered collapse of themselves; oak trees without being propped stand upright of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "High mountains fall without being struck down; oak trees rise without being braced up."

sentences.zh: 」令諜人多齎此文，遺之於鄴。

translations.literal: " He had spies carry many copies of this text and leave them at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He had agents carry many copies of the text and leave them in Ye.

sentences.zh: 祖孝徵既聞，更潤色之，明月竟以此誅。

translations.literal: When Zu Xiaozheng heard of it, he further embellished it; Mingyue was ultimately executed because of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Xiaozheng heard of it he polished the wording further, and Mingyue was eventually executed because of the rhyme.

sentences.zh: 建德之後，武帝志在平齊。

translations.literal: After the Jiande era, Emperor Wu set his mind on pacifying Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiande era Emperor Wu turned his mind to conquering Qi.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃上疏陳三策。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then submitted a memorial setting forth three strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan submitted a memorial presenting three strategies.

sentences.zh: 其第一策曰：

translations.literal: The first strategy said:
translations.idiomatic: The first strategy read:

sentences.zh: 臣在邊積年，頗見間隙，不因際會，難以成功。

translations.literal: Your minister has accumulated years on the frontier and has seen many openings; without seizing the occasion, success is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has spent years on the frontier and seen many openings. Without seizing the moment, success is hard.

sentences.zh: 是以往歲出軍，徒有勞費，功績不立，由失機會。

translations.literal: Therefore when troops went out in past years, there was only toil and expense; achievements were not established—because the opportunity was lost.
translations.idiomatic: That is why past campaigns cost labor and treasure yet won nothing—the moment was missed.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: For what reason?

sentences.zh: 長淮之南，舊為沃土，陳氏以破亡餘燼，猶能一舉平之。

translations.literal: South of the Long Huai was formerly fertile land; Chen with the embers of ruin and destruction could still level it in one campaign.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Long Huai was once rich country. Chen, already half ruined, still took it in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 齊人歷年赴救，喪敗而反，內離外叛，計盡力窮。

translations.literal: The men of Qi rushed to the rescue year after year, returned in defeat, inner separation and outer rebellion—their plans exhausted and strength spent.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent relief year after year and came back beaten. Within they split; without they rebelled. Their plans are spent and their strength gone.

sentences.zh: 傳不云乎：「讎有釁焉，不可失也。

translations.literal: Does not the tradition say: "When the enemy has a crack, it must not be missed"?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the classic say, "When the foe shows a crack, do not let it pass"?

sentences.zh: 」今大軍若出軹關，方軌而進，兼與陳氏共為掎角；

translations.literal: " Now if the great army sets out through Zhi Pass, advances in parallel columns, and together with Chen forms pincers;
translations.idiomatic: Now if the main army marches out through Zhi Pass in broad columns and joins Chen in a pincer;

sentences.zh: 并令廣州義旅，出自三鵶；

translations.literal: And orders Guangzhou righteous troops to sally from Sanya;
translations.idiomatic: if Guangzhou levies march from Sanya;

sentences.zh: 又募山南驍銳，沿河而下；

translations.literal: Also recruits fierce elites from south of the mountains to descend along the river;
translations.idiomatic: if fierce troops south of the mountains descend along the river;

sentences.zh: 復遣北山稽胡絕其並、晉之路。

translations.literal: Also sends northern-mountain Jie Hu to cut off their Bing and Jin routes.
translations.idiomatic: and if Jie Hu from the northern hills cut the roads through Bing and Jin—

sentences.zh: 凡此諸軍，仍令各募關、河之外勁勇之士，厚其爵賞，使為前驅。

translations.literal: All these armies—further order each to recruit stalwart warriors from beyond the Pass and the River, richly reward them with ranks and bounty, and make them vanguards.
translations.idiomatic: then let every force recruit bold men from beyond the Pass and the River, reward them richly, and send them ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 岳動川移，雷駭電激，百道俱進，竝趨虜庭。

translations.literal: Mountains move and rivers shift; thunder terrifies and lightning strikes; a hundred routes advance together and all rush toward the barbarians' court.
translations.idiomatic: Earth and water would seem to heave; thunder and lightning would terrify. A hundred columns would strike at once and drive straight for the enemy capital.

sentences.zh: 必當望旗奔潰，所向摧殄。

translations.literal: Surely they will flee at sight of banners; wherever [we] turn, they will be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: They would break at the sight of our flags and be crushed wherever we turned.

sentences.zh: 一戎大定，實在此機。

translations.literal: One campaign and great pacification—truly this is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: One stroke could settle the realm. The chance is now.

sentences.zh: 其第二策曰：

translations.literal: The second strategy said:
translations.idiomatic: The second strategy read:

sentences.zh: 若國家更為後圖，未即大舉，宜與陳人分其兵勢。

translations.literal: If the state plans further ahead and does not immediately launch a great effort, we should with Chen divide their military strength.
translations.idiomatic: If the court prefers a longer plan and will not strike at once, join Chen in splitting Qi's forces.

sentences.zh: 三鵶以北，萬春以南，廣事屯田，預為貯積。

translations.literal: North of Sanya, south of Wanchun—extensively practice garrison farming and prepare stores.
translations.idiomatic: From north of Sanya to south of Wanchun, expand garrison farming and build up stores.

sentences.zh: 募其驍悍，立為部伍。

translations.literal: Recruit their fierce and bold, and organize them into units.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit their hard fighters and form them into units.

sentences.zh: 彼既東南有敵，戎馬相持，我出奇兵，破其疆埸。

translations.literal: They, having an enemy in the southeast, horses of war locked in stalemate—we send surprise troops and break their borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: With an enemy in the southeast tying down their armies, we should raid their borders with surprise forces.

sentences.zh: 彼若興師赴援，我則堅壁清野，待其去遠，還復出師。

translations.literal: If they raise armies to rush to the rescue, we fortify walls and clear the countryside, wait until they have gone far, then march out again.
translations.idiomatic: If they march to relieve one point, we should fortify, strip the country bare, wait until they are far off, then strike elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 常以邊外之軍，引其腹心之眾。

translations.literal: Constantly use armies on the outer borders to draw their core forces.
translations.idiomatic: Always use frontier raids to pull their main armies away from the center.

sentences.zh: 我無宿舂之費，彼有奔命之勞。

translations.literal: We have none of the expense of overnight milling; they have the toil of emergency marches.
translations.idiomatic: We pay no cost of overnight grinding; they pay the price of forced marches.

sentences.zh: 一二年中，必自離叛。

translations.literal: In a year or two they will surely split and rebel of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In a year or two they will break apart on their own.

sentences.zh: 且齊氏昏暴，政出多門，鬻獄賣官，唯利是視，荒淫酒色，忌害忠良。

translations.literal: Moreover the Qi clan is dim and brutal; government issues from many gates; selling justice and selling offices, viewing profit alone; dissolute in wine and women, jealous and harming the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Qi is dark and cruel. Power comes from many hands. Offices and verdicts are for sale; profit is all they see. They drown in wine and women and destroy the loyal.

sentences.zh: 闔境熬然，不勝其弊。

translations.literal: The whole realm is in turmoil, unable to bear their abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm groans under them and cannot endure their rule.

sentences.zh: 以此而觀，覆亡可待。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, overthrow and ruin can be awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, their fall is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 然後乘間電掃，事等摧枯。

translations.literal: Then take the opening and sweep like lightning; the affair equals snapping dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: Then seize the opening and sweep them aside like lightning, as easily as breaking dry wood.

sentences.zh: 其第三策曰：

translations.literal: The third strategy said:
translations.idiomatic: The third strategy read:

sentences.zh: 竊以大周土宇，跨據關、河，蓄席捲之威，持建瓴之勢。

translations.literal: I venture that Great Zhou's territory spans and holds the Pass and the River, stores the might of rolling up [all under heaven] and holds the momentum of building from a high eave.
translations.idiomatic: Great Zhou holds the Pass and the River, with the power to roll up the realm and the momentum of a tide pouring from a high roof.

sentences.zh: 太祖受天明命，與物更新，是以二紀之中，大功克舉。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor received Heaven's bright mandate and renewed all things with them; therefore within two reign-periods great achievements were accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor received Heaven's mandate and renewed the age, and within two reign-periods great deeds were done.

sentences.zh: 南清江、漢，西龕巴、蜀，塞表無虞，河右底定。

translations.literal: South the Jiang and Han were cleared; west Ba and Shu were brought in; beyond the passes no worry; the right bank of the River was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The south was cleared to the Jiang and Han, the west brought in Ba and Shu, the frontier was secure, and the land west of the River was settled.

sentences.zh: 唯彼趙、魏，獨為榛梗者，正以有事三方，未遑東略。

translations.literal: Only those Zhao-Wei [territories] alone remain as brambles and blockages—precisely because there were affairs on three sides and no leisure for eastern advance.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhao and Wei remain as thorns in the side, because affairs on three fronts left no room to turn east.

sentences.zh: 遂使漳、滏遊魂，更存餘晷。

translations.literal: Thus the wandering souls by Zhang and Fu yet remain a little longer.
translations.idiomatic: So the lingering power by the Zhang and Fu rivers still survives a little longer.

sentences.zh: 昔勾踐亡吳，尚期十載；

translations.literal: Formerly Goujian destroyed Wu—he still looked to ten years;
translations.idiomatic: Goujian destroyed Wu only after ten years;

sentences.zh: 武王取亂，猶煩再舉。

translations.literal: King Wu took a chaotic [foe]—he still needed two efforts.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu overthrew the Shang only after two campaigns.

sentences.zh: 今若更存遵養，且復相時，臣謂宜還崇鄰好，申其盟約。

translations.literal: Now if we further preserve nurturing compliance and again wait for the right time, your minister holds we should restore honoring of neighborly good faith and renew the alliance treaty.
translations.idiomatic: If the court would rather nurture strength and bide its time, your servant holds we should honor good relations with our neighbor and renew the treaty.

sentences.zh: 安人和眾，通商惠工，蓄銳養威，觀釁而動。

translations.literal: Settle the people and harmonize the masses; open trade and benefit craftsmen; store sharpness and nurture majesty; watch for cracks and then act.
translations.idiomatic: Settle the people, keep trade open, benefit craftsmen, store up strength, and move only when a crack appears.

sentences.zh: 斯則長策遠馭，坐自兼并也。

translations.literal: This then is the long plan and distant governance—sitting and merging by oneself.
translations.idiomatic: That is the long strategy: govern from afar and absorb them without stirring.

sentences.zh: 書奏，武帝遣小司寇淮南西元

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; Emperor Wu sent Junior Minister of Crime Huainan Xi Yuan
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was in, Emperor Wu sent Junior Minister of Crime Yuan

translations.literal: (Wei) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: Wei]

sentences.zh: 〔偉〕、開府伊婁謙等重幣聘齊。

translations.literal: 〔Wei〕 [emended: Xi Yuan → Yuan Wei], Kaifu Yilou Qian, and others with heavy gifts to visit Qi as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, Kaifu Yilou Qian, and others with rich gifts to court Qi.

sentences.zh: 爾後遂大舉，再駕而定山東，卒如孝寬之策。

translations.literal: After that a great campaign was launched; twice the emperor took the field and settled the lands east of the mountains; in the end it happened as Xiaokuan's strategy [had said].
translations.idiomatic: Later the court did launch a great campaign. The emperor marched twice and pacified the east of the mountains, just as Xiaokuan had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 孝寬每以年迫懸車，屢請致仕。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan repeatedly, because his years pressed toward hanging up his chariot, asked many times to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan, feeling his years advance, repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝以海內未平，優詔弗許。

translations.literal: The emperor, because within the seas was not yet pacified, with a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, holding that the realm was not yet fully at peace, graciously refused each request.

sentences.zh: 至是復稱疾乞骸骨。

translations.literal: At this point he again claimed illness and requested to retire.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he again pleaded illness and asked to be allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「往已面申本懷，何煩重請也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You have already stated your intent to me in person — why trouble yourself with repeated requests?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You already told me your mind face to face — why ask again?

sentences.zh: 」五年，帝東伐，過幸玉壁。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year the emperor marched east; passing through, he visited Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year Emperor Wu marched east and, passing through, visited Yubi.

sentences.zh: 觀禦敵之所，深嘆羨之，移時乃去。

translations.literal: He viewed the places where the enemy had been held at bay, sighed deeply in admiration, and only after a long while departed.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the enemy's old defenses, sighed in deep admiration, and lingered a long while before leaving.

sentences.zh: 孝寬自以習練齊人虛實，請為先驅。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, judging himself practiced in the strengths and weaknesses of the men of Qi, asked to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan, who knew the Qi armies well, asked to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 帝以玉壁要衝，非孝寬無以鎮之，乃不許。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yubi was a vital choke point and none but Xiaokuan could hold it, would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Yubi was too vital to leave to anyone but Xiaokuan and refused.

sentences.zh: 及趙王招率兵出稽胡，與大軍掎角，乃敕孝寬為行軍總管，圍守華谷以應接之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhao Zhao led troops out against the Ji Hu in pincer coordination with the main army, he thereupon ordered Xiaokuan to be campaign commander, to besiege and hold Huagu in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Yuwen Zhao marched against the Ji Hu in pincer with the main force, Xiaokuan was ordered to act as campaign commander, besiege Huagu, and keep the link open.

sentences.zh: 孝寬克其四城。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan captured four of their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan took four of their cities.

sentences.zh: 武帝平晉州，復令孝寬還舊鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Jin Province, he again ordered Xiaokuan back to his old garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took Jin Province, Xiaokuan was sent back to his former post.

sentences.zh: 及帝凱還，復幸玉壁。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned in triumph, he again visited Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: On his triumphant return the emperor visited Yubi again.

sentences.zh: 從容謂孝寬曰：「世稱老人多智，善為軍謀。

translations.literal: At ease he said to Xiaokuan: "The world calls old men wise and skilled in military planning.
translations.idiomatic: At his ease he said to Xiaokuan, "People say old men are wise and full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 然朕唯共少年，一舉平賊。

translations.literal: Yet I worked only with the young and in one stroke leveled the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I relied on the young alone and crushed the enemy in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 公以為何如？

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you make of that?"

sentences.zh: 」孝寬對曰：「臣今衰耄，唯有誠心而已。

translations.literal: " Xiaokuan replied: "Your servant is now decrepit; I have nothing but sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaokuan answered, "I am old now and have little left but loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然昔在少壯，亦曾輸力先朝，以定關右。

translations.literal: Yet in my youth I too once lent strength to the former court and helped settle the Guan-right region.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my prime I too served the former court and helped secure the country west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑曰：「實如公言。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed greatly and said: "It is truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "That is exactly so.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔孝寬隨駕還京。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Xiaokuan to follow the imperial retinue back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Xiaokuan to return to the capital with the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 拜大司空，出為延州總管，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Minister of Works, sent out as area commander of Yan Province, and advanced to Upper Pillar-of-State.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand minister of works, posted as area commander of Yan Province, and raised to upper pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 軍還，至豫州，宇文亮舉兵反，潛以數百騎襲孝寬營。

translations.literal: As the army returned and reached Yuzhou, Yuwen Liang raised troops in rebellion and secretly sent several hundred horsemen in a surprise attack on Xiaokuan's camp.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home, at Yuzhou, Yuwen Liang rebelled and sent several hundred riders in a night raid on Xiaokuan's camp.

sentences.zh: 時亮圉官茹寬密白其狀，孝寬有備。

translations.literal: At the time Liang's household official Ru Kuan secretly reported the situation; Xiaokuan was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's household officer Ru Kuan got word to him in secret, and Xiaokuan was ready.

sentences.zh: 亮不得入，遁走，孝寬追獲之。

translations.literal: Liang could not enter, fled, and Xiaokuan pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang failed to break in, fled, and Xiaokuan ran him down and captured him.

sentences.zh: 詔以平淮南之功，別封一子滑國公。

translations.literal: An edict, for the merit of pacifying Huainan, separately enfeoffed one son Duke of Hua State.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Huainan an edict separately enfeoffed one of his sons as Duke of Hua.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝崩，隋文帝輔政，時尉遲迥先為相州總管，詔孝寬代之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died and Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) assisted the government, Yuchi Jiong was then area commander of Xiang Province; an edict ordered Xiaokuan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died and Yang Jian, later Emperor Wen of Sui, took power as regent, Yuchi Jiong was area commander of Xiang Province; Xiaokuan was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 又以小司徒叱列長文為相州刺史，先令赴鄴。

translations.literal: Chilie Zhangwen was also made Lesser Minister of Reckoning and Inspector of Xiang Province, and was first sent on ahead to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Chilie Zhangwen was also made lesser minister of reckoning and inspector of Xiang Province and sent on ahead to Ye.

sentences.zh: 孝寬續進，至朝歌，迥遣大都督賀蘭貴齎書候孝寬。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan pressed on and, reaching Chaoge, Jiong dispatched Grand Commander Helan Gui bearing a letter to inquire after Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan continued forward; at Chaoge, Yuchi Jiong sent Grand Commander Helan Gui with a letter of greeting.

sentences.zh: 孝寬留貴與語以察之，疑其有變，遂稱疾徐行。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan kept Gui to talk and observe him, suspected there would be a change, and thereupon claimed illness and traveled slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan detained Gui for conversation to probe him, suspected treachery, and feigned illness to slow his march.

sentences.zh: 又使人至相州求醫藥，密以伺之。

translations.literal: He also sent men to Xiang Province to seek medicines, secretly to spy on events.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent men to Xiang Province ostensibly to obtain medicines, but in secret to watch what was happening.

sentences.zh: 既到湯陰，逢長文奔還。

translations.literal: Having reached Tangyin, he met Zhangwen fleeing back.
translations.idiomatic: At Tangyin he met Zhangwen fleeing back toward him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬兄子魏郡守藝又棄郡南走。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's elder brother's son Yi, Administrator of Wei commandery, also abandoned the commandery and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan's nephew Yi, administrator of Wei commandery, had likewise abandoned his post and fled south.

sentences.zh: 孝寬審訐其狀，乃馳還。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan verified the treacherous situation and thereupon galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiaokuan confirmed the plot, he galloped back at once.

sentences.zh: 所經橋道，皆令毀撤，驛馬悉擁以自隨。

translations.literal: Every bridge and road he passed he ordered destroyed; all relay horses he gathered to accompany himself.
translations.idiomatic: Every bridge and road on his route was torn up, and every relay horse was taken along for his own use.

sentences.zh: 又勒

translations.literal: He also ordered
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed

translations.literal: (Qí) [emended: Yì]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Yì]

sentences.zh: 〔驛〕將曰：「蜀公將至，可多備餚酒及芻粟以待之。

translations.literal: 〔Yì〕 station commanders, saying: "The Duke of Shu is about to arrive — prepare plenty of food and wine and fodder to await him.
translations.idiomatic: the relay-station commanders, "The Duke of Shu is coming — lay in rich food, wine, and fodder for him.

sentences.zh: 」迥果遣儀同梁子康將數百騎追孝寬，驛司供設豐厚，所經之處，皆輒停留，由是不及。

translations.literal: " Jiong indeed sent Yitong Liang Zikang with several hundred horsemen in pursuit of Xiaokuan; the relay offices supplied lavish provisions, and at every place they passed they always halted, so they could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuchi Jiong did send Yitong Liang Zikang with several hundred riders after Xiaokuan, but the relay stations feasted them so generously that they halted everywhere and never caught up.

sentences.zh: 時或勸孝寬，以為洛京虛弱，素無守備，河陽鎮防，悉是關東鮮卑，迥若先往據之，則為禍不小。

translations.literal: Some at the time urged Xiaokuan, arguing that the Luoyang capital was weak and had long lacked defenses, that the Heyang garrison was entirely eastern Guan Xianbei, and that if Jiong went first to seize it the harm would be no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Xiaokuan that Luoyang was weak and undefended, that Heyang was held by eastern Guan Xianbei, and that if Yuchi Jiong seized it first the damage would be grave.

sentences.zh: 乃入保河陽。

translations.literal: He thereupon entered and fortified Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore withdrew into Heyang and held the city.

sentences.zh: 河陽城內舊有鮮卑八百人，家並在鄴，見孝寬輕來，謀欲應迥。

translations.literal: Within Heyang city there were formerly eight hundred Xianbei whose families were all in Ye; seeing Xiaokuan come lightly, they plotted to respond to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred Xianbei garrison troops in Heyang, with families in Ye, saw Xiaokuan arrive with a small force and plotted to join Yuchi Jiong.

sentences.zh: 孝寬知之，遂密造東京官司，詐稱遣行，分人詣洛陽受賜。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan learned of it and thereupon secretly sent word to the Eastern Capital offices, falsely claiming he was dispatching men on mission and dividing them to go to Luoyang to receive rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan learned of the plot and secretly notified the Eastern Capital authorities, pretending to send men on official business to Luoyang to receive gifts.

sentences.zh: 既至洛陽，並留不遣。

translations.literal: Once they reached Luoyang, all were detained and not released.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Luoyang they were all detained.

sentences.zh: 因此離解，其謀不成。

translations.literal: Because of this they were dispersed and the plot did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: That broke up the conspiracy before it could succeed.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔發關中兵，以孝寬為元帥東伐。

translations.literal: In the sixth month an edict mobilized Guanzhong troops and made Xiaokuan commander for the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict raised Guanzhong armies and made Xiaokuan supreme commander of the eastern expedition.

sentences.zh: 七月，軍次河陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the army encamped at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the army halted at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 迥所署儀同薛公禮等圍逼懷州，孝寬遣兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Xue Gongli and other Yitong appointed by Jiong pressed and besieged Huaizhou; Xiaokuan sent troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Gongli and other Yitong officers under Yuchi Jiong besieged Huaizhou; Xiaokuan sent troops and routed them.

sentences.zh: 進次懷縣永〔橋〕城

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Huai county's Yong
translations.idiomatic: He moved up and encamped southeast of Yong

translations.literal: (Qiáo) [emended: Qiáo]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Qiáo]

sentences.zh: 之東南。

translations.literal: city to the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Bridge city in Huai county.

sentences.zh: 其城既在要衝，雉堞牢固，迥已遣兵據之。

translations.literal: That city lay on a vital pass; its battlements were strong, and Jiong had already sent troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: The town stood on a key route, its walls were strong, and Yuchi Jiong had already garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 諸將士以此城當路，請先攻取。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, because this city blocked the road, asked to attack and take it first.
translations.idiomatic: His officers, seeing the town in the way, asked to reduce it first.

sentences.zh: 孝寬曰：「城小而固，若攻而不拔，損我兵威。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan said: "The city is small yet strong; if we attack and cannot take it, we will damage our army's prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan said, "The place is small but tough; if we attack and fail, we lose face.

sentences.zh: 今破其大軍，此亦何能為也。

translations.literal: Now if we break their great army, what can this place do?"
translations.idiomatic: Break their main force and this town can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 」於是引軍次于武陟，大破迥子惇，惇輕騎奔鄴。

translations.literal: " He thereupon drew up the army at Wuzhi and greatly defeated Jiong's son Dun; Dun fled to Ye with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " He then encamped at Wuzhi and routed Yuchi Jiong's son Dun, who fled to Ye with a small mounted band.

sentences.zh: 軍次於鄴西門豹祠之南。

translations.literal: The army encamped south of the Leopard Shrine at Ye's west gate.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted south of the Leopard Shrine at Ye's west gate.

sentences.zh: 迥自出戰，又破之。

translations.literal: Jiong came out himself to give battle and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong came out to fight in person and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 迥窮迫自殺。

translations.literal: Jiong, driven to extremity, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Yuchi Jiong took his own life.

sentences.zh: 兵士在小城中者，盡坑於遊豫園。

translations.literal: The soldiers in the lesser cities were all buried alive in Youyu Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The troops still holding the outlying towns were buried alive in Youyu Garden.

sentences.zh: 諸有未服，皆隨機討之，關東悉平。

translations.literal: Wherever any had not yet submitted, all were dealt with as occasion demanded, and the Guandong region was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Holdouts were mopped up as opportunity allowed, and the whole Guandong region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十月，凱還京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he returned in triumph to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 十一月薨，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died; he was then seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅、十二州諸軍事、雍州牧。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Tutor, military affairs of twelve provinces, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor, commander of military affairs in twelve provinces, and governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 諡曰襄。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 孝寬在邊多載，屢抗強敵。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan spent many years on the frontier and repeatedly withstood strong enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan served long on the frontier and repeatedly faced formidable enemies.

sentences.zh: 所有經略，佈置之初，人莫之解；

translations.literal: In all the strategies he laid out, at the beginning of their deployment no one understood them;
translations.idiomatic: At first no one understood the plans he laid;

sentences.zh: 見其成事，方乃驚服。

translations.literal: only when they saw the outcome accomplished were they then amazed and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: only when they succeeded did men marvel and submit.

sentences.zh: 雖在軍中，篤意文史，政事之餘，每自披閱。

translations.literal: Though in the army, he devoted himself to literature and history; in the spare time left from government affairs he always read for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Even in camp he kept to books and history, reading on his own whenever duty allowed.

sentences.zh: 末年患眼，猶令學士讀而聽之。

translations.literal: In his later years he suffered from eye disease, yet still had scholars read aloud for him to listen.
translations.idiomatic: When his eyes failed in old age, he still had scholars read aloud to him.

sentences.zh: 又早喪父母，事兄嫂甚謹。

translations.literal: He also lost his parents early and served his elder brother and sister-in-law with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was scrupulously dutiful to his elder brother and sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 所得俸祿，不入私房。

translations.literal: The salary he received did not enter his private rooms.
translations.idiomatic: He never kept his official salary for private use.

sentences.zh: 親族有孤遺者，必加振贍。

translations.literal: If any among his kin were orphaned and left behind, he always added relief and support.
translations.idiomatic: Any orphaned kin he always supported.

sentences.zh: 朝野以此稱焉。

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 長子諶年已十歲，魏文帝欲以女妻之。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chen was already ten years old; Emperor Wen of Wei wished to give him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When his eldest son Chen was ten, Emperor Wen of Wei wanted to marry a princess to him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬辭以兄子世康年長。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan declined on the ground that his elder brother's son Shikang was older.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan declined, citing his elder brother's son Shikang, who was older.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，遂以妻世康。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this and thereupon gave the princess to Shikang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and gave the princess to Shikang instead.

sentences.zh: 孝寬有六子，總、壽、霽、津知名。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan had six sons; Zong, Shou, Ji, and Jin were the ones of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had six sons; Zong, Shou, Ji, and Jin were the best known.

sentences.zh: 韋敻字敬遠。

translations.literal: Wei Xiong, styled Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong, courtesy name Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 志尚夷簡，澹於榮利。

translations.literal: His aspirations were lofty and plain; he was indifferent to glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: He aspired to simplicity and cared nothing for rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，被召拜雍州中從事，非其好也，遂謝疾去職。

translations.literal: At the capping age he was summoned and appointed Assistant Clerk of Yong Province; it was not to his liking, and he thereupon claimed illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was summoned as assistant clerk of Yong Province, disliked the post, claimed illness, and resigned.

sentences.zh: 前後十見徵辟，皆不應命。

translations.literal: Before and after, on ten occasions he was summoned and recruited, yet he never accepted appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Ten times he was called to office; ten times he refused.

sentences.zh: 屬太祖經綸王業，側席求賢，聞敻養高不仕，虛心敬悅，遣使辟之，備加禮命。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was organizing the royal enterprise, he sat aside from his seat seeking the worthy; hearing that Xiong lived in lofty retirement and would not serve, he sincerely admired and delighted in him, sent envoys to recruit him, and added full honors and commissions.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was building the dynasty he sought talent with special urgency; learning that Xiong lived in honorable retirement, he admired him sincerely, sent envoys to recruit him, and offered the fullest honors.

sentences.zh: 雖情諭甚至，而竟不能屈。

translations.literal: Though feelings were explained to the utmost, in the end he could not be bent.
translations.idiomatic: They reasoned with him at length, but he could not be moved.

sentences.zh: 彌以重之，亦弗之奪也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai only valued him the more and also did not take the office away from him by force.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai only respected him the more and would not force him from his chosen life.

sentences.zh: 所居之宅，枕帶林泉，敻對翫琴書，蕭然自樂。

translations.literal: The dwelling where he lived backed on forests and springs; Xiong, facing them, played the qin and read books, desolate and self-content.
translations.idiomatic: His house lay among woods and streams; there Xiong played the qin, read, and lived content in quiet seclusion.

sentences.zh: 時人號為居士焉。

translations.literal: People of the time called him the Layman.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day called him the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 至有慕其閑素者，或載酒從之，敻亦為之盡歡，接對忘倦。

translations.literal: Some who admired his leisurely simplicity would even carry wine and follow him; Xiong also fully enjoyed himself with them, meeting and conversing until weariness was forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Admirers of his plain life sometimes brought wine and kept him company; Xiong welcomed them gladly and talked on without tiring.

sentences.zh: 陳遣其尚書周弘正來聘，素聞敻名，請與相見。

translations.literal: Chen sent its Minister Zhou Hongzheng on a friendly mission; having long heard Xiong's name, he asked to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Minister Zhou Hongzheng on a diplomatic visit; having long known Xiong's reputation, he asked to meet him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷許之。

translations.literal: The court permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 弘正乃造敻，談謔盈日，恨相遇之晚。

translations.literal: Hongzheng thereupon visited Xiong; they talked and jested a full day, regretting that they had met so late.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng called on Xiong; they talked and bantered all day and lamented that they had met so late in life.

sentences.zh: 後請敻至賓館，敻〔不〕時赴。

translations.literal: Later he invited Xiong to the guest lodge; Xiong [did not] arrive on time.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked Xiong to the guesthouse; Xiong [did not] come promptly.

sentences.zh: 弘正仍贈詩曰：「德星猶未動，真車詎肯來。

translations.literal: Hongzheng thereupon presented a poem saying: "The star of virtue has not yet moved — how would the true carriage deign to come?
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng sent him a poem: "The star of virtue has not yet stirred — would the true carriage condescend to come?

sentences.zh: 」其為時所欽挹如此。

translations.literal: " He was admired and looked up to by the age to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which his contemporaries held him.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗與敻夜宴，大賜之縑帛，令侍臣數人負以送出。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once held a night banquet with Xiong and greatly bestowed silk and brocade on him, ordering several attending ministers to carry it on their backs and escort him out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once feasted with Xiong at night and gave him a great pile of silk and brocade, ordering several attendants to carry it out after him.

sentences.zh: 敻唯取一疋，示承恩旨而已。

translations.literal: Xiong took only one bolt, to show that he accepted the grace of the edict and no more.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong took only one bolt, enough to acknowledge the gift and no more.

sentences.zh: 帝以此益重之。

translations.literal: The emperor for this valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor respected him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 孝寬為延州總管，敻至州與孝寬相見。

translations.literal: When Xiaokuan was area commander of Yan Province, Xiong came to the prefecture and met Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaokuan was area commander of Yan Province, Xiong visited the prefecture and met him.

sentences.zh: 將還，孝寬以所乘馬及轡勒與敻。

translations.literal: About to return, Xiaokuan gave him the horse he rode and its bridle.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong was leaving, Xiaokuan gave him his own horse and harness.

sentences.zh: 敻以其華飾，心弗欲之。

translations.literal: Xiong, because of its ornate trappings, in his heart did not wish for it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong disliked the showy trappings and did not want the gift.

sentences.zh: 笑謂孝寬曰：「昔人不棄遺簪墜履者，惡與之同出，不與同歸。
