translations.literal: Smiling, he said to Xiaokuan: "Men of old did not discard a lost hairpin or a fallen shoe, hating to set out together yet not return together.
translations.idiomatic: Smiling, he told Xiaokuan, "The ancients would not leave behind a lost hairpin or a dropped shoe, for they hated to go out together and come back apart.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不逮前烈，然捨舊錄新，亦非吾志也。

translations.literal: Though I do not reach the former worthies, yet to cast aside the old and record the new is also not my aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: I am no sage of old, but to discard what is mine and take what is new is not my way either.

sentences.zh: 」於是乃乘舊馬以歸。

translations.literal: " He thereupon rode his old horse and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He rode his old horse home.

sentences.zh: 武帝又以佛、道、儒三教不同，詔敻辨其優劣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also, because the Three Teachings of Buddhism, Daoism, and Confucianism differed, ordered Xiong to distinguish their relative merits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu also, finding Buddhism, Daoism, and Confucianism at odds, ordered Wei Xiong to judge which excelled.

sentences.zh: 敻以三教雖殊，同歸於善，其迹似有深淺，其致理殆無等級。

translations.literal: Xiong held that though the Three Teachings differ, they alike return to goodness; their traces seem to have depth and shallowness, yet in reaching principle there is scarcely any gradation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong held that though Buddhism, Daoism, and Confucianism differ, they all lead to goodness; their outward paths may seem deep or shallow, but in principle they stand on no ladder of rank.

sentences.zh: 乃著三教序奏之。

translations.literal: He thereupon composed a Preface to the Three Teachings and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote a Preface to the Three Teachings and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and commended it.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝在東宮，亦遺敻書，并令以帝所乘馬迎之，問以立身之道。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was in the Eastern Palace; he also sent Xiong a letter, and ordered that the emperor's own mount be sent to welcome him, asking about the way to establish oneself in life.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Crown Prince, later Emperor Xuan, was in the Eastern Palace; he too wrote to Wei Xiong, sent the emperor's own horse to fetch him, and asked how a man should stand in life.

sentences.zh: 敻對曰：「傳不云乎，儉為德之恭，侈為惡之大。

translations.literal: Xiong replied: "Does not the Classic say: Frugality is the reverence of virtue; extravagance is the root of many evils.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong replied, "Does not the Classic say, 'Frugality is the reverence of virtue; extravagance is the root of many evils.

sentences.zh: 欲不可縱，志不可滿。

translations.literal: Desires must not be indulged; the will must not be filled.
translations.idiomatic: Desires must not be indulged, and the will must not be filled.

sentences.zh: 竝聖人之訓也，願殿下察之。」

translations.literal: These are alike the sage's teachings—I hope Your Highness will ponder them."
translations.idiomatic: These are the sage's teachings alike—I hope Your Highness will weigh them."

sentences.zh: 敻子瓘行隨州刺史，因疾物故，孝寬子總復於并州戰歿。

translations.literal: Xiong's son Guan was acting governor of Sui Prefecture and died of illness; Xiaokuan's son Zong also fell in battle at Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong's son Guan, acting governor of Sui, died of illness, and Wei Xiaokuan's son Zong was killed in battle at Bing.

sentences.zh: 一日之中，凶問俱至。

translations.literal: Within a single day, tidings of both deaths arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single day news of both deaths arrived.

sentences.zh: 家人相對悲慟，而敻神色自若。

translations.literal: The household faced one another in grief and lamentation, yet Xiong's expression remained as usual.
translations.idiomatic: The household wept together, but Wei Xiong's face stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 謂之曰：「死生命也，去來常事，亦何足悲。

translations.literal: He said to them: "Life and death are fate; coming and going are ordinary affairs—what is there worth grieving over?
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "Life and death are fate; coming and going are ordinary things—what is there to mourn?

sentences.zh: 」援琴撫之如舊。

translations.literal: " He took up the zither and played it as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He took up his zither and played as before.

sentences.zh: 敻又雅好名義，虛襟善誘。

translations.literal: Xiong also by nature loved reputation and righteousness; with open mind he was good at guiding others.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong also loved honor and righteousness by nature, and with an open mind he guided others well.

sentences.zh: 雖耕夫牧豎有一介可稱者，皆接引之。

translations.literal: Even if a plowman or cowherd had the least merit worth praising, he would all receive and lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Even a plowman or cowherd with the smallest merit worth noting he would take in and encourage.

sentences.zh: 特與族人處玄及安定梁曠為放逸之友。

translations.literal: He especially counted his clansman Chuxuan and Liang Kuang of Anding as friends in free and easy living.
translations.idiomatic: He counted his clansman Chuxuan and Liang Kuang of Anding especially among his friends in an easy, unforced life.

sentences.zh: 少愛文史，留情著述，手自抄錄數十萬言。

translations.literal: In youth he loved literature and history; he devoted attention to writing and personally copied out several hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved literature and history, kept at writing, and copied out several hundred thousand words in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 晚年虛靜，唯以體道會真為務。

translations.literal: In his later years he was empty and still; he took embodying the Way and meeting truth as his sole task.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he lived in quiet detachment and made embodying the Way and grasping truth his only pursuit.

sentences.zh: 舊所制述，咸削其藁，故文筆多竝不存。

translations.literal: What he had formerly composed and set down, he all cut away the drafts of, so most of his writings no longer survive.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed the drafts of everything he had written, so most of his writings no longer survive.

sentences.zh: 建德中，敻以年老，預戒其子等曰：「昔士安以蘧蒢束體，王孫以布囊繞尸，二賢高達，非庸才能繼。

translations.literal: In Jiande, Xiong, because of old age, beforehand admonished his sons and others, saying: "Formerly Shi'an bound his body with coarse reed matting, and Wang Sun wrapped the corpse in a cloth bag—those two worthies were lofty and far-reaching; no ordinary talent could follow them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiande era, grown old, Wei Xiong warned his sons in advance: "Long ago Lu Ji bound his body in coarse reed matting and Wang Sunchu wrapped the corpse in a cloth bag—those two sages were lofty men no ordinary person could imitate.

sentences.zh: 吾死之日，可斂舊衣，勿更新造。

translations.literal: On the day I die, you may dress me in old clothes; do not make new ones.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, dress me in old clothes; do not have new ones made.

sentences.zh: 使棺足周尸，牛車載柩，墳高四尺，壙深一丈。

translations.literal: Let the coffin be just enough to enclose the body; let an ox cart carry the bier; let the mound be four chi high and the vault one zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: Let the coffin barely fit the body, let an ox cart carry the bier, let the mound rise four chi and the vault go one zhang deep.

sentences.zh: 其餘煩雜，悉無用也。

translations.literal: All the rest of the troublesome and elaborate—altogether useless.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else elaborate and troublesome is useless.

sentences.zh: 朝晡奠食，於事彌煩，吾不能頓絕汝輩之情，可朔望一奠而已。

translations.literal: Morning and evening offerings of food would only make the affair more burdensome; I cannot abruptly cut off your feelings—one offering at new moon and full moon will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening food offerings would only burden you; I cannot ask you to cut off your feelings all at once—offer once at new moon and full moon only.

sentences.zh: 仍薦素蔬，勿設牲牢。

translations.literal: Still offer plain vegetables; do not set out sacrificial livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Offer plain vegetables only; do not set out sacrificial livestock.

sentences.zh: 親友欲以物弔祭者，並不得為受。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends wishing to bring goods for mourning sacrifice—all must not have them accepted on my behalf.
translations.idiomatic: If kin and friends wish to bring goods for mourning sacrifice, you must not accept them for me.

sentences.zh: 吾常恐臨終恍惚，故以此言預戒汝輩。

translations.literal: I have often feared that at the end I might be confused; therefore I use these words beforehand to admonish you.
translations.idiomatic: I have often feared I might lose my wits at the end, so I warn you of this in advance.

sentences.zh: 瞑目之日，勿違吾志也。」

translations.literal: On the day my eyes close, do not violate my intent."
translations.idiomatic: When I close my eyes, do not go against my wishes."

sentences.zh: 宣政元年二月，卒於家，時年七十七。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xuanzheng, he died at home, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xuanzheng year 1 he died at home, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣使祭，賻賵有加。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent envoys to sacrifice; funeral gifts and condolence offerings were added.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent envoys to perform the sacrifice, and added generous funeral gifts and condolence offerings.

sentences.zh: 其喪制葬禮，諸子等並遵其遺戒。

translations.literal: As for mourning rites and burial ceremony, the sons and others all followed his testamentary admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: His sons and the rest carried out the mourning and burial exactly as his last instructions commanded.

sentences.zh: 子世康。

translations.literal: His son was Shikang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shikang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 梁士彥字相如，安定烏氏人也。

translations.literal: Liang Shiyan, styled Xiangru, was a man of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan, courtesy name Xiangru, came from Wushi in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 少任俠，好讀兵書，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and bold; he loved reading military books and broadly touched on the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and chivalrous, loved military texts, and had a fair grounding in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 周武帝將平東夏，聞其勇決，自扶風郡守除為九曲鎮將，進位上開府，封建威縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was about to pacify Eastern Xia, hearing of his courage and decisiveness, he removed him from Fufeng commandery administrator to make him commander of Jiuqu garrison, advanced him to upper opener-of-office, and enfeoffed him Duke of Jianwei county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou was preparing to pacify Eastern Xia, he heard of Liang Shiyan's courage and made him commander of Jiuqu garrison in place of his post as administrator of Fufeng, raised him to upper opener-of-office, and enfeoffed him Duke of Jianwei.

sentences.zh: 齊人甚憚之。

translations.literal: The men of Qi greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Qi feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，轉亳州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui directed the government, he was transferred to overall commander of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui directed the government, Liang Shiyan was made overall commander of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥反，為行軍總管，及韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, he was made campaigning commander-in-chief and joined Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, he was made campaigning commander-in-chief and marched with Wei Xiaokuan against him.

sentences.zh: 令家僮梁默等為前鋒，士彥繼之，所當皆破。

translations.literal: He ordered household retainers Liang Mo and others to serve as vanguard; Shiyan followed after; wherever they met the enemy, all were broken.
translations.idiomatic: He put household retainers Liang Mo and others in the vanguard and followed behind; every enemy line they met was broken.

sentences.zh: 及迥平，除相州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jiong was pacified, he was appointed governor of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuchi Jiong was crushed, he was made governor of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 深見忌，乃代還京師。

translations.literal: Deeply mistrusted, he was replaced and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply mistrusted, he was recalled to the capital and replaced.

sentences.zh: 閒居無事，恃功懷怨，與宇文忻、劉昉等謀反。

translations.literal: Idle at home with nothing to do, relying on his merit yet harboring resentment, he plotted rebellion with Yuwen Xin, Liu Fang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Idle at home, he leaned on past merit and nursed a grudge, and with Yuwen Xin, Liu Fang, and others plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 將率僮僕，候上享廟之際以發機。

translations.literal: He would lead servants and retainers, waiting for when the sovereign attended the temple sacrifice to launch the plot.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to lead his servants and retainers and strike when the emperor went to the ancestral temple for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 復欲於蒲州起事，略取河北，捉黎陽關，塞河陽路，劫調布為牟甲，募盜賊為戰士。

translations.literal: He also wished to raise the affair at Pu Prefecture, seize Hebei in brief, take Liyang Pass, block the Heyang road, seize tax cloth for armor padding, and recruit bandits as fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: He also meant to raise forces at Pu, overrun Hebei, seize Liyang Pass, block the Heyang route, requisition tax cloth for armor padding, and enlist bandits as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其甥裴通知而奏之。

translations.literal: His nephew Pei Tong learned of it and memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Pei Tong learned of the plot and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝未發其事，授晉州刺史，欲觀其志。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reveal the matter; he appointed him governor of Jin Prefecture, wishing to observe his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the matter secret, made him governor of Jin Prefecture, and watched to see what he would do.

sentences.zh: 士彥欣然謂昉等曰：「天也！

translations.literal: Shiyan said joyfully to Fang and the others: "Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan said delightedly to Liu Fang and the others, "Heaven itself!

sentences.zh: 」又請儀同薛摩兒為長史，帝從之。

translations.literal: " He also requested Equal-in-protocol Xue Mo'er as chief clerk; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked for Equal-in-protocol Xue Mo'er as chief clerk, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 後與公卿朝謁，帝令執士彥、忻、昉等於行間。

translations.literal: Later, when he attended court audience with the high ministers, the emperor ordered Shiyan, Xin, Fang, and the others seized in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a court audience with the high ministers, the emperor had Liang Shiyan, Yuwen Xin, Liu Fang, and the others seized in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 詰之狀，猶不伏，捕薛摩兒至，對之。

translations.literal: When the charges were put to them, they still would not confess; Xue Mo'er was captured and brought; they were confronted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned under charge, they still would not confess; Xue Mo'er was brought in and they were confronted with him.

sentences.zh: 摩兒具論始末，云第二子剛垂泣苦諫，第三子叔諧曰「作猛獸須成班」。

translations.literal: Mo'er fully set forth the beginning and end, saying the second son Gang wept and bitterly admonished, and the third son Shuxie said, "To make a fierce beast, you need a full group."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Mo'er told the whole story, saying the second son Gang wept and pleaded against the plot, while the third son Shuxie said, "To make a fierce beast you need a full band."

sentences.zh: 士彥失色，顧曰：「汝殺我！

translations.literal: Shiyan changed color and, turning, said: "You have killed me!
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shiyan turned pale and cried out, "You have killed me!

sentences.zh: 」於是伏誅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then executed.

sentences.zh: 年七十二。

translations.literal: He was seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 有子五人。

translations.literal: He had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons survived him.

sentences.zh: 操字孟德，位上開府、義鄉縣公，早卒。

translations.literal: Cao, styled Mengde, held the rank of upper opener-of-office and Duke of Yixiang county; he died early.
translations.idiomatic: Cao, courtesy name Mengde, held upper opener-of-office and was Duke of Yixiang; he died young.

sentences.zh: 剛字永固，位大將軍、通政縣公、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Gang, styled Yonggu, held the rank of grand general, Duke of Tongzheng county, and governor of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gang, courtesy name Yonggu, was grand general, Duke of Tongzheng, and governor of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以諫父獲免，徙瓜州。

translations.literal: Because he admonished his father, he was spared; he was transferred to Gua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had admonished his father, he was spared and exiled to Gua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 叔諧坐士彥誅。

translations.literal: Shuxie was implicated in Shiyan's execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxie was executed along with Liang Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 梁默者，士彥之蒼頭也，驍武絕人。

translations.literal: Liang Mo was Shiyan's household slave; his martial valor surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Mo was Liang Shiyan's household slave and a fighter without peer.

sentences.zh: 士彥每從征伐，常與默陷陣。

translations.literal: Whenever Shiyan followed on campaigns, he always broke the enemy lines together with Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liang Shiyan went on campaign, he and Liang Mo broke enemy lines together.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位開府。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he reached the rank of opener-of-office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Zhou he rose to opener-of-office.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，以行軍總管從楊素征突厥，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, as campaigning commander-in-chief he followed Yang Su in campaigning against the Türks and was advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era he served as campaigning commander-in-chief under Yang Su against the Türks and was raised to grand general.

sentences.zh: 又從平楊諒，授柱國。

translations.literal: He again followed in pacifying Yang Liang and was granted pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in crushing Yang Liang and was made pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，從煬帝征吐谷渾，力戰死之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, following Emperor Yang in the campaign against Tuyuhun, he fought hard and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 5 he followed Emperor Yang against Tuyuhun, fought hard, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
